# Agent Friendly Web

> Public website auditor and guided owner workspace created by Gabriel Mucchiut and incubated within Tokenizart.

Agent Friendly Web measures public evidence about how agents can discover, understand, and use a website. Its AF-0 to AF-5 framework is a proprietary methodology published for transparent use; it is not an official certification.

## Important limits

- Public scans are read-only and do not authenticate to the target website.
- `llms.txt` is a community proposal, not a mandatory crawler standard.
- WebMCP is treated as an experimental W3C Community Group draft.
- The private owner dossier requires sign-in and must not be crawled or inferred.
- The repo-first read-only CLI and the public stateless MCP read-only server are deployed. MCP exposes only four bounded public tools and four public resources; A2A, WebMCP and x402 are not production capabilities.
- The AI Catalog links the OKF bundle as an Agent Friendly Web project convention; OKF v0.2 does not define a universal discovery endpoint.
